title: Race calculator
trip.label: Trip
trip.hint: Required: rests and pacing differ a lot between the two
trip.tip: Guided group: the main number is the time your past group days' EP/h give, with your capacity time beside it; on your own: the main number is your capacity time (your walking capacity at AeT: the steep walking windows of your trail runs plus the climbing windows of Baiyue (Taiwan's 100 Peaks) hikes at HR ≥ AeT).
calc.tip: A red * is required. Once everything is filled in, every change recalculates on its own; Calculate recalculates right away. With a season-plan event selected, the inputs and result are saved with that event and come back the next time you pick it.
chart.title: Segment targets
chart.tip:
Each segment's target pace, power or heart rate along the course.
How to read: distance (km) across, one measure up; the light area is the elevation profile; hover the chart or click the table for a segment's details.
Look for: flats and runnable climbs (3–8 %) by power; steep (> 8 %) or walked climbs by an HR cap; trail descents by neither (control and safety), so they are blank on the power / HR chart; on races > 3 h the HR cap is AeT.
Method: the grade models set each segment's target.
safe: Descent: no power or HR target — control and safety
legend.gap_power: gap on the chart = power is only a reference here (steep, descent; grey in the table)
legend.gap_hr: gap on the chart = HR is only a reference on trail descents (grey in the table)
map.hint: hover the map or the profile to see the same point on both; switch basemaps top right
env.title: Conditions
env.tip: From = your usual training conditions (where your power was measured): the median altitude of your last 90 days of runs, temperature and humidity from the historical weather of those runs, else the median of all your activities. To = race day: with an event, date and place (peak, coordinates or the GPX start) the forecast is fetched on its own (CWA → Open-Meteo); a date too far ahead uses the 5-year climatology. The difference becomes the environment factor M. Press ✎ to change them.
env.adv: Advanced: change From / To yourself (blue = changed by you; clear to go back to automatic)
env.to_wait: fetched once a date and place are set
env.need_date: fetched once the race date is set
env.need_loc: fetched once a place (peak, coordinates) or a GPX course is set
env.none: No automatic data; press ✎ to fill it in
coros.title: Export to plan
coros.tip: Writes this race's legs as one session on race day in your training plan: edit each step on the Schedule page, then push it to the watch from there. On trails the watch's distance is often off (switchbacks, tree cover), so trail and Baiyue (Taiwan's 100 Peaks) exports end every step with the lap button: press lap at the place the step names (aid station, top or bottom of a climb); the name also gives the predicted time and climb. On a road GPS is fine, so road exports use distance steps. Each step's target follows the segment targets: power ± 3 %; steep and walked climbs only an HR cap (no estimated power; open when there is no cap); none on trail descents. Baiyue exports carry heart rate only (no power, no pace); a multi-day Baiyue trip cannot be exported, only a single-day one. The estimated TSS counts legs without a target at the calculator's predicted race HR ÷ LTHR; after each race it is compared with the actual TSS for a personal correction (close to 1 with few races). One session per race: exporting again overwrites the last export.
coros.same: The plan already has this version
coros.claim: replaces the plan's “Race” session on that day
coros.restored: you deleted this session from the plan; it will be added back
coros.edited: This session was changed on the Schedule page: exporting overwrites your changes
coros.confirm_overwrite: This race session was changed on the Schedule page; exporting overwrites your changes. Overwrite?
coros.need_event: Pick the target race first: the export goes on that race's day
coros.push_hint: Once it is in the plan, push it to the watch from the Schedule page
coros.old_watch: The watch has this race from an earlier direct export: it is replaced the next time this session is pushed from the plan
coros.tss_hr: legs without a target at IF {f} ({src})
coros.tss_default: no HR prediction: legs without a target at the default IF {f}
coros.tss_nocalib: no post-race correction yet (compared with the actual TSS after each race)
pick.title: Pick a location on the map
pick.hint: Click the map to drop a marker; drag it to fine-tune. Switch basemaps top right. A click within 300 m of a known peak also takes the peak's elevation.
goal.tip: Enter the goal as a pace (average pace or finish time) or as a power (average power in W or % CP): both are offered. The per-km / segment targets are spread from your goal by the grade model. No goal = the model's own prediction.
goal.vs_tip: Model = the 「model prediction」 time (100 % effort) on the same course and weather. Faster by more than 3 % is flagged, by more than 8 % warned; the thresholds are an estimate.
goal.fast: {pct}% faster than the model: may not hold
goal.too_fast: {pct}% faster than the model: likely won't hold
zbar.axis_power: Palladino; axis = % CP, line = this race's average power
zbar.axis_hr: axis = heart rate in bpm, line = this race's predicted average heart rate
zbar.tip: This bar shows absolute intensity: which of your zones the race's average power or heart rate falls in. The effort bar above shows relative intensity: how long you can hold this power, which depends on the race length — 85% CP is easy for 1 hour and hard for 8 hours. Each colour is a zone (each zone's name and range are listed below); the line is this race's average. Power training shows power zones, heart-rate training shows heart-rate zones (the training basis in Settings); you can pick the heart-rate zone model, the default is the workout heart-rate zones in Settings.
zbar.line_power: Absolute intensity: average {pct} CP ({w}), in Palladino zone {zone}
zbar.line_hr: Absolute intensity: average {hr} bpm, in {sys} zone {zone}
zbar.no_hr_data: This calculation has no average heart rate, so the power zones are shown
cad.title: Climbing cadence
cad.how: Counts only moving time with cadence on the 100 m stretches of 3 % or steeper, in your outdoor runs of the last year. Every walk / run split in the app is “cadence below 130 spm = walking”; on climbs cadence usually falls into a walking and a running group, and the line should sit in the valley between them. This only checks; it never moves the line.
rw.title: Walk–run transition speed
rw.default: Default values, none of your data yet: a grade needs at least 10 walked and 10 run windows.
rw.personal: Your transition speed is {d} m/s off the default ({n} windows, shrunk towards the default). The calculator's walk / run labels use it.
rw.how: Slower than the line, walking costs less; faster, running does. The default line comes from treadmill tests on high-level male runners (Brill & Kram 2021, Ortiz 2017); using it for everyone is an estimate. Your line: for every 2 % of grade, the speed at which half of your own 100 m windows are walked and half run; the median difference from the default, shrunk towards 0 by sample size and held within ±0.4 m/s (all estimates). Heart-rate crossovers are not used.
rw.legend_default: walk / run labels: default transition speed
rw.legend_you: walk / run labels: your transition speed
sg.line: Walk or run by the predicted speed (SP-229, not used in predictions yet): trail segment |error| {a} → {b}, climbs {c} → {d} ({n} segments, gait changed on {k}).
sg.no: worse: predictions keep the majority gait
